title: Food Facts
blurb: Strange but true stories from the kitchen, the farm and the snack aisle.

prompts.text: Before Dutch growers made orange ones popular, cultivated carrots were mostly purple or _____.
Apples float in water because about a quarter of their volume is _____.
The pistachio belongs to the same plant family as the cashew and the _____.
Botanically, almonds are the seeds of a fruit closely related to the _____.
Nachos were invented in 1943 in a Mexican town just across the border from _____.
According to the official story, the ice block on a stick was invented by accident in 1905 by a boy aged _____.
Alongside dark, milk and white, a fourth type of chocolate launched in 2017 is _____ chocolate.
Rhubarb stalks are great in a crumble, but the leaves are poisonous thanks to _____ acid.
Kiwifruit used to be sold under the name Chinese _____.
Natural vanilla comes from the seed pods of a type of _____.
The man who designed the Pringles can had some of his ashes buried in a _____.
Bananas are very slightly radioactive because of the _____ they contain.
Hawaiian pizza was invented in 1962 in _____.
German chocolate cake isn't German at all: it's named after Samuel _____, who created the chocolate it uses.
The holes in Swiss cheeses like Emmental are officially called _____.
An Italian bank accepts wheels of _____ as security for business loans.
Kopi luwak, one of the world's priciest coffees, is made from beans that have been eaten and passed by the _____.
Gummy bears were invented in 1922 by Hans Riegel, the founder of _____.
Fanta was first made in _____ during the Second World War, when Coca-Cola syrup couldn't be imported.
When it launched in 1929, the drink that became 7 Up contained _____, now used as a psychiatric medicine.
In 1943 the United States briefly banned the sale of _____ to save resources during the war.
Durian smells so strong that it is banned on Singapore's _____.
Casu marzu, a traditional cheese from Sardinia, is deliberately full of live _____.
Cheddar cheese takes its name from a village in the English county of _____.
Birds can't feel the burn of chilli, so they happily eat the fruit and spread its _____.
Nutella grew out of a paste made in post-war Italy, where chocolate was scarce, by stretching it with _____.
Fresh pineapple stops jelly from setting because it contains _____, an enzyme that breaks down protein.
The country that grows the most cocoa in the world is _____.
Potatoes, tomatoes and eggplants all belong to the same plant family as deadly _____.
Ancient Romans splashed a fermented fish sauce called _____ on almost everything.
Ripe cranberries are sorted from bad ones by testing how well they _____.
Raw red kidney beans contain a toxin, so they must be properly _____ before eating.
Corn Flakes were first created as a plain health food at a Michigan _____.
Coca-Cola was invented in 1886 in Atlanta by the pharmacist John _____.
In 1893 the US Supreme Court ruled that, for import tariff purposes, tomatoes are legally _____.
Pepsi-Cola was first sold in the 1890s under the name _____.
Most bananas sold today are Cavendish, which replaced the once-dominant Gros _____ after a fungal disease struck.
Tabasco sauce has been made since the 1860s on Avery Island in _____.
In 1957 the BBC fooled viewers with an April Fools report about spaghetti being harvested from _____.
Marmite is a spread made from yeast left over as a by-product of _____ brewing.
The sharp bite of black pepper comes from a compound called _____.
Mushrooms are not plants; biologically they are closer to _____.
Saffron threads are the dried stigmas of a type of _____.
